title: Latency budgeting for ephemeral inference and trace sample guidelines
content:
Context and motivation:

This note collects an operationally practical approach to defining latency budgets for ephemeral inference workloads and an associated trace-sampling plan that keeps trace costs bounded while preserving signal for oncall and postmortem. 'Ephemeral inference' here = short-lived, low-token chats, heavy fanout of small model calls, and lots of cold-KV-cache cases (typical for new customers, canaries, and first-request UX).

Goals:
- Ensure tail-latency SLOs capture cold-cache and microbatch behavior without blowing trace budget.
- Produce a small set of dashboard panels that quickly surface cold-cache tails, prefetch misses, and multi-model fanout path regressions.
- Define a severity-weighted sampling scheme so we collect traces where they help debugging most.

High-level latency budget model (layers):
1) Client-to-edge (network + LB): budget 30–60ms for NA regions (depends on customer SLA).
2) Edge-to-runtime (routing + auth + tokenization): budget 10–40ms.
3) Inference runtime hot path (first-token-to-last-token across model variants): primary budget slice, default target 200ms for short requests (<128 tokens), scaled up for longer flows.
4) KV cache warmness and prefetch: separate micro-SLO: median KV-hit-rate >= 85% for hot cohorts; tail KV-miss fraction must be <2% for production tenants.
5) Aggregation & fanout stitching: budget 30–100ms depending on number of model calls and allowed parallelism.

Notes on allocation:
- Keep budget arithmetic simple: use percentiles that match operator needs (50p/95p/99p). E.g., if overall 95p budget for short requests is 300ms, allocate 180ms to runtime, 60ms to routing+tokenization, 60ms to edge+network.
- For canaries and new tenants, apply a temporary relaxed budget for the overall SLO but add stricter sub-SLOs on KV-hit-rate and fanout path correctness to avoid masking cold cache issues.

Metric definitions (examples):
- metric: inference.request.latency_ms (tags: tenant_id, model_variant, request_type, kv_hit)
  - description: total end-to-end latency measured at ingress (ms)
  - example query: SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) FROM inference_requests WHERE request_type='chat' AND model_variant='m1-small';

- metric: inference.runtime.encode_latency_ms, inference.runtime.decode_latency_ms
  - capture tokenizer and model compute slices so runtime allocation is visible.

- metric: kv.prefetch.hit_rate (tags: tenant_id, shard)
  - description: fraction of prefix/KV requests that hit in LRU cache within 1s. Helpful for cold-cache investigation.

- metric: fanout.call.count and fanout.call.latency_ms (tags: path_id, step_index)
  - track per-request fanout graph: number of downstream calls and the slowest child latency.

Trace sampling plan (practical):
Principle: combine deterministic sampling on critical flows with severity-weighted probabilistic sampling, and small reservoir sampling for background.
- Deterministic always-sample for:
  - any request that triggers an automatic fallback (model fallback, region fallback, quantization fallback)
  - any request that hits an explicit error code (5xx runtime, model OOM)
  - onboarding/canary tenants flagged in metadata
- Severity-weighted sampling for latencies:
  - latency < p95: sample 0.2% (background)
  - p95 <= latency < p99: sample 10%
  - latency >= p99: sample 100%
- KV-miss amplification: if kv.prefetch.hit_rate=false for request, multiply the sampling probability by 4 (min cap 5%) to ensure cold-cache traces are visible.
- Fanout-path heuristic: if fanout.call.count > 3, increase sampling by factor 2; if combined fanout latency contribution > 30% of end-to-end, force sample.
- Budgeting: cap total trace collection at X traces/min per region (TBD per infra cost), with soft throttles that drop lowest-severity background samples when the cap is hit.

Trace envelope & retention heuristics:
- Keep standard traces at compact size: only include full proto stack for sampled high-severity traces; for background traces, store only span timing + small context (request id, tenant, model_variant, kv_hit flag, top-3 slow spans).
- For forced-sampled traces (fallbacks/errors), store full payload for 72 hours then expire to compressed index.

Dashboard and alert sketches (operator-first):
Panel set A — rapid triage (compact single row):
- Single-line: 95p inference.request.latency_ms for production tenants (small sparkline)
- KV warmth panel: rolling kv.prefetch.hit_rate (1h window) with stripe highlights for tenants below 80%
- Cold-tail alarm: 99p latency increases > 2x baseline over 30m window -> fire P1 oncall signal
- Fanout map: heatmap of fanout.call.count vs average end-to-end latency (helps detect expensive graph shapes)

Panel set B — investigation deep slice (click-through):
- Session reconstruction: top N slow requests with trace-links, kv_hit flag
- Span waterfall generator: show runtime encode/decode/kv spans for suspect requests
- Error basket: grouped by fallback type + sample trace links

Operator playbook bullets (quick):
- First check: is the 99p spike concentrated in a small tenant cohort? If yes, look at kv.prefetch.hit_rate and tenant deployment variant.
- Second: check fanout.call.count and which step_index contributes the most latency.
- Third: open quick trace link (forced-sampled preferred). If no trace, expand sampling window for that tenant and repro traffic in sandbox.

Open questions and TODOs:
- Choose numeric cap T (traces/min) per region and run 2-week experiment to tune sampling multipliers. (JIRA-OBS-4127)
- Add tenant-level pre-warming policy and expose prewarm diagnostics in customer console (product/solutions ask).
- Small experiment: keep a 1% reservoir of full-sized traces for background traffic for 24h to evaluate if compact envelopes lose critical debug info.

References and quick links:
- Linked artifacts above (Confluence & JIRA) for cost calc and prior experiments.
- Slack thread: #obs-latency (see pinned messages re: 2025-09 trial)

Appendix: short checklist for rollout to prod:
- [ ] Implement sampling multipliers in trace router (config flag with rollout gate).
- [ ] Create dashboard sheets (A + B) and a small runbook card for oncall.
- [ ] Run 2-week shadow mode capturing sampling counts and cost impact, review with infra finance.
- [ ] Iterate thresholds after initial data (expect tuning of kv amplification factor).

Notes to self: rough heuristics above, don't bake numbers until we have a region-by-region cost model. Keep dashboard minimal at first (one compact row and 3 drill-through widgets).
